$comment: Reference questions for `bun run eval`. Values come from data/lol.sqlite (schema v6, full scope, in-game stats from the Riot JSON on Leaguepedia as of 2026-11-14); key totals were cross-checked with independent SQL on the base tables. `expect` fields: route (tool name, sql or out_of_scope), players / teams / champion (resolved names, order matters), league (Leaguepedia League), input (subset of the tool input), rows (exact count) or rowsMin (minimum), totals (subset of answer.meta.totals), ambiguity ({mention, chosen, alternatives (subset)}), attempts, notes (substrings), sources (minimum count, Leaguepedia links). Timeline questions read the Riot JSON from R2 (R2_READ_*) or, locally, from data/raw/riot; without either their totals.timeline is "unconfigured". Checks that need a query result are skipped when the route is sql and no OPENROUTER_API_KEY is set. `now` is the date relative seasons are resolved against ("l'an dernier" = 2025). `expect.unread` lists the words the rules did not understand when they put the route in doubt (answer.meta.unread). A case marked `llm: true` needs the LLM to reach its expected route (the rules hand it to the LLM router): without a key only its rules-level checks run (steps, players, teams, champion, unread) and it is reported as needing the LLM, not as passed. The `paraphrase` cases are the 30 questions of the routing audit of 2026-11-14, the `variant` cases their variants. The `champion` and `lane` cases (2026-11-14) cover the champion profile and ranking tools and the role leaderboards; their key totals were cross-checked with independent SQL on the base tables. The `roster` cases (2026-11-14) cover the team roster tool (players by role over a period, renamed teams merged); their game counts were cross-checked with independent SQL on the base tables. The `pool` cases (2026-11-14) cover the champion pool of a player or a team (champion_pool tool); their key totals were cross-checked with independent SQL on the base tables. The `pool` cases tagged `alias` (2026-11-14) cover the short and reordered ways to ask for a champion pool ("pool champ bin", "bin champ pool", "pool bin", near typos); their key totals were cross-checked with independent SQL on v_game_players. The `items` cases (2026-11-15) cover a champion's end-of-game items (Leaguepedia ScoreboardPlayers.Items, Data Dragon kinds); the first dragon cases show the count beside the share. Their key totals were cross-checked with independent SQL on the base tables, and the MSI 2023 game counts per team with gol.gg. `worlds-chovy-closed` (2026-11-15) is the question the Data release workflow asks the new database: closed editions only, so its totals hold on fresh data; cross-checked with independent SQL on game_players (regional qualifiers excluded). Expectations that include the Worlds 2026 final (4 games, Bilibili Gaming 3-1 Gen.G, 2026-11-14) were updated on 2026-11-15 to the data-20261115 release; the final standings of an edition still in progress are covered by scripts/architecture.test.ts. The `empty` case (2026-11-17) is an empty result the scope explains (src/lib/agent/empty.ts): a player's only games on a champion in regional qualifiers (Faker on Azir, LCK 2024 Regional Finals, shown as the answer's one row); cross-checked with independent SQL on v_game_players.
